content: New pulleys are taller than the old ones, in case they get mixed together.
I seem to have missed getting the right panel off to have access to the motor. I removed it.

I might recommend using the spacer tool indicated when putting the new gear on the motor shaft to verify if the spacing on the old gear matches the spacer.  When complete, I had an issue with one of the motors where the gear did not align with the pulley if I used the spacer and had to eye ball the spacing to get a success on  X and Y tests.
Can these replaced pulleys be reused on the MK4S?  Shame if we toss it.
I had a square nut fall out in this step.  be careful!
I was able to do the next section without cutting the zip tie, but it was harder. You decide

replies.content: I also left the zip tie. If doing the INDX conversion at the same time, leaving the zip tie was fine since the tube isn't in the way.

content:
From experience I know that once the grub screws have been tightened on the motor shaft that it is almost impossible to remove the pulley without applying significant pulling force to overcome the friction caused by displaced metal where the grub screws have bitten into the shaft.

Will this cause damage to the motor?

replies.content: Had the same issue and was also wondering if that could damage the motor?
